newsitem.title: USA: Apple South sees 96 eps below estimates.
newsitem.headline: Apple South sees 96 eps below estimates.

text.p: Apple South Inc said on Tuesday that its 1996 earnings would fall short of analysts estimates of $0.95 per share because of a sluggish restaurant environment and management turnover.
Apple South said in a statement that its earnings would still be modestly above last year's results, before merger and asset revaluation charges.
The casual dining restaurant company earned $0.73 per share in its last fiscal year.
Third quarter results would reflect a previously announced $6 million pre-tax or $0.10 per share charge for the closure of Tomato Rumba's Pastaria Grill, it said.
But Apple South said it expected to return to 33 percent earnings growth rate next year.
Chairman and Chief Executive Officer Tom DuPree said Apple South was reducing its development schedule for the next two years and taking steps to remedy staffing shortages.
"I decided that we needed a jolt to hasten the process and get us back on track for intermediate and long-term success for our guests, our employees and our investors," he said in a statement.
DuPree said a culture clash at an acquisition in the midwest had led to an increase in management turnover.
He said the company's Don Pablo division average unit volume continued to grow at a 40 percent rate and margins there were expanding.
Apple South operates a total of 297 restaurants.
